title: How to re-order and upsert records after combining two dataframes
question:

|    def|s_system3|s_feed3|        s_para_3|  s_run_gp3|sflag_3|         s_pipe3|
|    bcz|s_system2|s_feed2|        s_para_2|  s_run_gp2|sflag_2|s_pipe2_upadated|
|    fjk|s_system4|s_feed4|        s_para_4|  s_run_gp4|sflag_4|         s_pipe4|
|    dfg|s_system5|s_feed5|        s_para_5|  s_run_gp5|sflag_5|         s_pipe5|

|103|    def|s_system3|s_feed3|        s_para_3|  s_run_gp3|sflag_3|   s_pipe3|
+---+-------+---------+-------+----------------+-----------+-------+----------+

Here I want to insert the new record from the SourceDF with the incremental id. If the records are updated, then I need to update in the target table. The id in the TargetDF is consistent. So if records in the SourceDF are wrongly placed, then it should re-order and update in the target table.

The case is:

  1. Record with s_gp - "bcz" which stands with id - 205 as per TargetDF has wrongly placed in SourceDF. But with updated value "s_pipe2_upadated", so when updating into the target table, the order should be corrected - i.e. it should update against 205 only.
  2. If it is a completely new record in SourceDF as per TargetDF, then it should insert as new record.

answer:
try this

from pyspark.sql import functions as F
from pyspark.sql.window import Window
join_cols = [col for col in source_df.columns if col in target_df.columns and col != "id"]
print("Join columns", join_cols)
matched_df = source_df.join(
    target_df.select("id", *join_cols),
    on=join_cols,
    how="left"
)
existing_records_df = matched_df.filter(F.col("id").isNotNull())
print("existing_records_df")
display(existing_records_df)
source_with_key = source_df.withColumn("join_key", F.concat_ws("||", *join_cols))
target_with_key = target_df.withColumn("join_key", F.concat_ws("||", *join_cols))
updated_or_new_df = source_with_key.join(
    target_with_key.select("id", "s_line", "join_key"),
    on="join_key",
    how="left"
).filter(
    (F.col("id").isNull()) | (F.col("s_line") != F.col("target_with_key.s_line"))
).drop("join_key", "target_with_key.s_line")
print("updated_or_new_df")
display(updated_or_new_df)
max_id = target_df.select(F.max("id")).first()[0] or 0
window = Window.orderBy(F.monotonically_increasing_id())
new_records_with_ids = updated_or_new_df.withColumn(
    "id", F.row_number().over(window) + max_id
)
print("new_records_with_ids")
display(new_records_with_ids)
final_df = target_df.alias("tgt").join(
    new_records_with_ids.alias("src"), on="id", how="left_anti"
).unionByName(new_records_with_ids)
final_df = final_df.orderBy("id")
print("Final merged TargetDF")
display(final_df)
